notes.text: Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen.
Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin.
Mattias Ekholm returned in their last game after missing 2 games.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 44% of the team’s power-play time in 13 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 3% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, down from 30% last season.
Eeli Tolvanen is away for personal reasons, reported after he played in their last game.
Scott Morrow has not played this season.
Taylor Raddysh was added to the roster on Oct 17 and has played beside Justin Dowling and Oliver Bjorkstrand.
Luke Glendening was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Taylor Raddysh and Eeli Tolvanen.
James Reimer was added to the roster on Oct 26.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Rangers are on a three-game losing streak, while the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. The Oil played last night, and the Rangers are rested. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Rangers fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 16th).
The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing. The Rangers’ record (.536) is about what their chances are worth.

The Oilers (lowest) and the Rangers (3rd lowest) both lean hard on their top players. The Oilers have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.23 goals a game, the most in the league. As for the Rangers, they get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Rangers’ power play (7th) could do real damage against the Oilers’ penalty kill (23rd). On top of that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 28 A / 36 P in 13 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with 13 points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 13 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games. For the Rangers, Adam Fox (1 G / 16 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 14 GP) has a team-high nine goals, tied for seventh in the NHL.
Matt Tomkins will likely start for Edmonton, his first start of the season, and Dylan Garand (4-5-1 / .899 SV% in 8 GS) for the Rangers.
